title: I built a free breakout alert tool with stackable confirmation filters (RVOL, ATR, RSI, multi-timeframe) — looking for honest feedback
author: hroob777
selftext:
I've been building trading tools on the side for a while, and the one I use most myself is a breakout watcher. Sharing it here because I think this sub would give me the most useful, unfiltered feedback — good or bad.

**What it does:**  
You set a support/resistance level (or let it pull pivot points automatically), pick how you want to be alerted, and it monitors price in real time. When it triggers, you get a sound alert in-browser or a Telegram alert (so you don't need the tab open).

**Three alert modes:**

* Fixed price — classic level touch/close
* Price × Moving Average — alerts when price crosses an EMA/SMA
* MA Cross — Golden Cross / Death Cross detection (fast MA vs slow MA)

**The part I actually care about your opinion on — Advanced Filters:**  
Raw breakout alerts are noisy, so I built stackable filters that sit on top of any of the three modes:

* **RVOL** — only fires if breakout volume is X× the 20-candle average
* **ATR** — only fires if the candle's range is X× the average candle size (filters weak moves)
* **RSI range** — block overbought/oversold entries or confirm momentum
* **EMA side filter** — price has to be on the correct side of an EMA/SMA (no buying resistance breaks into a downtrend)
* **Candle body %** — ignores wick-driven "breakouts" with tiny real bodies
* **Consecutive candle confirmation** — requires N candles closing beyond the level before it counts

You can combine as many of these as you want. If a filter blocks a signal, it still logs it with the exact reason (e.g. "blocked: RVOL 1.1x < 1.5x required") so you can see what almost triggered and why it didn't.

There's also an optional multi-timeframe check (15m confirms against 1h, 1h against 4h, etc.) and a 5-candle retest window after a confirmed break.

**Link:** [https://www.cryptofxradar.com/p/breakout-watcher-tool.html](https://www.cryptofxradar.com/p/breakout-watcher-tool.html)

It's fully free, no signup required to try it (Telegram connection is optional, just for alerts when the page is closed).

Genuinely want to know: does the filter stack make sense the way I've set it up, or is there an obvious confirmation combo I'm missing? Also curious if anyone finds the RVOL/ATR thresholds I picked (1.2x–3x, 0.5x–2x) reasonable defaults or if I'm off base. Happy to take criticism — this is a hobby project, not trying to sell anything.

comments.author: Beginning_Support_86
comments.body:
the most useful thing in this tool is the thing you described in one line and moved past: you log blocked signals with the reason they were blocked.



almost every alerter throws away what it suppresses. yours keeps it, which means you are one column short of a dataset. add the forward outcome to every logged row, fired and blocked alike, say price at +5, +20 and +60 candles from the trigger. then your two questions stop being design questions and become queries.



right now "does the filter stack make sense" is not answerable by anyone, including someone with a lot of experience, because you have six stackable filters with continuous thresholds on top of three modes plus a multi-timeframe check. that is thousands of combinations. any answer i gave you would be taste. and if you tune the combo by watching recent price action, you are building an overfitting machine with a nice ui, because filters that fit the last two months always look good on the last two months.



the blocked signals are what makes it escapable. they are your control group. a filter is only worth having if the signals it killed did worse than the ones it let through, and you are the only person who can measure that because you are the only one keeping them.



on the thresholds specifically, 1.2-3x RVOL and 0.5-2x ATR are unobjectionable and also unjustifiable, same as any other numbers anyone would name. two weeks of logging with outcomes attached and you will not have to ask.



one thing to watch when you do run it: every filter you stack reduces the number of signals, and a smaller sample makes the survivors look better whether or not the filter helped. always report the count next to the hit rate, and treat a combo that fires nine times in three months as unmeasured rather than good.

replies.author: hroob777
replies.body:
One thing worth clarifying — the filters aren't meant to be stacked all at once. The idea is that different traders have different edges, so the tool gives them the options and they pick what fits their setup. Someone trading breakouts on high volume sessions has different needs than someone looking for clean EMA reclaims.

That said, the overfitting point is valid and I agree with it. If you turn everything on and tune to recent price action you're just fitting the last two months. The fix is what you said — log the outcomes at +5, +20, +60 candles for both fired and blocked signals, then the thresholds justify themselves or they don't. Already planning to add that.

The "one column short of a dataset" framing actually reframed how I think about the signal log. Appreciate the breakdown, genuinely useful.

replies.author: Beginning_Support_86
replies.body:
fair correction, and you are right that offering options is not the same as prescribing a stack. i saw six filters and jumped to someone turning them all on.



the thing worth thinking about though is that the search does not disappear when it moves to the user, it just gets distributed. if a trader tries eight or ten combinations against their own recent window and keeps whichever looked best, that is the same selection procedure, only now it runs once per user with nobody positioned to correct it. and the ones who land on a lucky combo are the ones who write you a testimonial, so the feedback reaching you is filtered by precisely the effect you would want to measure.



which is where the outcome log becomes more than a validation tool. once you have +5 / +20 / +60 for fired and blocked signals, you can compute the correction for them instead of hoping they know to ask for it. show the chosen combo's hit rate next to the distribution of hit rates across every combo on the same data. if theirs sits at the 60th percentile of all combos, that is the honest read and it is one chart. if it sits outside the whole spread, they have found something real and can now believe it.



i have not seen an alerter that does that. it is a differentiator hiding inside a bug fix, and you are about two weeks of logging away from being able to ship it.

replies.author: hroob777
replies.body:
That's the part I hadn't fully thought through — the selection pressure doesn't go away, it just moves to the user side and becomes invisible. And you're right that the feedback loop is broken by construction, the ones who write testimonials are exactly the ones who got lucky on their combo.

The percentile framing is what makes it actionable though. Showing someone their chosen combo's hit rate next to the distribution of all combos on the same data is a completely different thing than just showing them their win rate. If they're at the 60th percentile, they know. If they're outside the spread, they know that too. One chart, honest read.

That's actually a better product than the alerter itself. And like you said, it's two weeks of logging away. The outcome columns are already the missing piece — everything else follows from having +5, +20, +60 on both fired and blocked signals.

Didn't expect this thread to turn into a product roadmap but here we are. Appreciate it.

replies.author: Beginning_Support_86
replies.body: one build note for when you get there, because it is the easy thing to get wrong and it is invisible when you do.

replies.author: hroob777
replies.body:
That's the exact mistake I would have made and not caught until someone pointed it out. Computing the percentile on the same window the combo was tuned on inflates the whole distribution and makes everything look more meaningful than it is.

The out-of-sample split is the right fix and you're right that the timestamps make it straightforward — log the signals with dates, fix a split point, rank on the later window only. One date parameter in the background and the chart becomes honest.

Noted. Will build it that way from the start.
